chapter: New Orleans bands, players and halls
title: Rough uptown halls and trumpeters Harrison Gougie and Ogin
summary: Foster describes the Funky Butt, Big Easy and Number 12 halls and trumpeters Harrison Gougie and Ogin.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, the quadrilles people, it wasn't a rough thing. See, most of them dancers uptown they had two different classes. People would come early part of the night, they'd leave like the cooks would take those at night. Well the rough ones would come in after 12 o'clock, they wouldn't come in until after 12 o'clock because they wasn't going to play no blues. See? Now back in those days if a band couldn't play no blues, man, uptown they could play them rough halls like the Funky Butt Hall. See? They used to play a hall called the Big Easy Hall. What was that, Big Easy?

That's in the Grittner. Oh. Go over to Grittner and play the Big Easy. Now like the first... Big Easy and they come clean. Big Easy and they come clean. See? And then they had another one over there called the number 12. See? Well they give dances every Saturday night. They hold about 50 people I believe. And they made money. You get a glass of beer like that for nickel, wine for nickel, sell you dinner. They made money. And everybody was happy. Well the first band we had a trumpet player called Harrison Gougie. You remember Gougie? His old daddy had that Schumacher shop back on Duvern Street. See? Absolutely. Yeah. See? Harrison could play everything he see but he couldn't play in nothing, so he don't listen to look at the music. He was just a straight shot. He just learnt my music. See? He didn't have no... No. He didn't know...
That was Harrison Barnes or something?

Oh. Harrison Gougie. I know. That's what I'm saying. That's just what I'm saying right now. That's just what I'm saying right now. I'm glad you brought man because we could think of some people. Then we have another Creole boy called Ogin. Ogin? Ogin. From way down on, Mary Sugar refiner played trumpet, hold his head down and played some of the sweet... He wasn't no high note man but he played some of the nicest stuff with the old ugly hooker guy. Oh. Yeah. They don't write with those guys. They don't know. Yeah, nobody's heard of. You see, you see now, I should write a book myself. Should've done write a book. Yeah, he's good. He knows people. You see, we're getting back to the guys who work in the district. You see. Now Bunk, Bunk got so bad around, it ruined Bunk when he went with the Eagle band. When he was down there with the Superior band down there with the Creole boys it was very nice. So when he got uptown, that's when he started drinking in the battle house and stayed up all night. A guy called Franky Dusen. He'd end up all night. For months and months Bunk didn't go home, sleep on the pool table, time to go play.
